nodes.name: $\ell_p$ ball / Compressibility class $X_{p,m}(R)$
nodes.statement: For $0<p<2$ and $R>0$, $X_{p,m}(R)=\{x: \|\theta(x)\|_p \le R\}$ where $\theta_i=\langle x,\psi_i\rangle$ are transform coefficients in an orthonormal basis $(\psi_i)$ and $\|\theta\|_p \equiv (\sum_i |\theta_i|^p)^{1/p}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Class of objects whose transform coefficients have bounded $\ell_p$ norm; encodes sparsity for small $p$.

nodes.name: Information operator $I_n$
nodes.statement: A nonadaptive linear map $I_n: X \mapsto \mathbb{R}^n$ of the form $I_n(x)=(\langle \xi_1,x\rangle,\ldots,\langle \xi_n,x\rangle)$, where the sampling kernels $\xi_i$ are fixed independently of $x$.

nodes.name: Minimax $\ell_2$ reconstruction error $E_n(X)$
nodes.statement: $E_n(X)=\inf_{A_n,I_n} \sup_{x\in X} \|x-A_n(I_n(x))\|_2$, the optimal worst-case $\ell_2$ error over all nonadaptive information operators $I_n$ and reconstruction algorithms $A_n$.

nodes.name: Adaptive minimax error $E_n^{\mathrm{Adapt}}(X)$
nodes.statement: $E_n^{\mathrm{Adapt}}(X)=\inf_{A_n,I_n^A} \sup_{x\in X} \|x-A_n(I_n^A(x))\|_2$, where $I_n^A$ allows each kernel $\xi_{i,x}$ to depend on previously observed measurements.

nodes.name: Gel'fand $n$-width $d^n(X;\ell_2)$
nodes.statement: $d^n(X;\ell_2)=\inf_{V_n} \sup\{\|x\|_2: x\in V_n^{\perp}\cap X\}$, where the infimum is over $n$-dimensional linear subspaces $V_n \subset \mathbb{R}^m$.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_n(X;\ell_2)$
nodes.statement: $d_n(X;\ell_2)=\inf_{V_n} \sup_{x\in X}\inf_{y\in V_n}\|x-y\|_2$, the best worst-case $\ell_2$-approximation of $X$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace $V_n$.

nodes.name: Width relative to operator $w(\Phi,X)$
nodes.statement: $w(\Phi,X) \equiv \sup\{\|x\|_2: x\in X\cap \ker(\Phi)\}$, the radius of the section of $X$ cut out by $\ker(\Phi)$.

nodes.name: Quotient norm $Q_{J^c}$
nodes.statement: $Q_{J^c}(v)=\min \|\theta\|_{\ell_1(J^c)}$ subject to $\Phi_{J^c}\theta=v$; the minimal $\ell_1$-norm representation of $v$ using only columns of $\Phi$ outside $J$.

nodes.name: CS matrix conditions CS1-CS3
nodes.statement: An $n\times m$ matrix $\Phi$ is a CS matrix with parameters $(\eta_i,\rho)$ if uniformly in $|J|<\rho n/\log(m)$: (CS1) $\sigma_{\min}(\Phi_J) > \eta_1$; (CS2) $\|v\|_1 \ge \eta_2 \sqrt{n}\,\|v\|_2$ for all $v\in V_J$; (CS3) $Q_{J^c}(v) \ge \eta_3/\sqrt{\log(m/n)}\,\|v\|_1$ for $v\in V_J$.

nodes.name: Concentration $\nu(\Phi,J)$
nodes.statement: $\nu(\Phi,J)=\sup\{\|1_J \beta\|_1/\|\beta\|_1 : \Phi\beta=0\}$, the maximal fraction of $\ell_1$ mass any nullspace vector can place on $J$.

nodes.name: Weak $\ell_p$ ball
nodes.statement: Vectors $\theta$ whose decreasing rearrangement $|\theta|_{(N)}$ obeys $|\theta|_{(N)} \le R \cdot N^{-1/p}$ for all $N\ge 1$. The smallest such $R$ defines $\|\theta\|_{w\ell_p}$, satisfying $\|\theta\|_{w\ell_p}\le \|\theta\|_p$.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-isometry between $\ell_2(J)$ and $\ell_1^n$
nodes.statement: $\Phi_J$ offers an $\epsilon$-isometry if $(1-\epsilon)\|\alpha\|_2 \le \sqrt{\pi/(2n)}\,\|\Phi_J \alpha\|_1 \le (1+\epsilon)\|\alpha\|_2$ for all $\alpha\in \mathbb{R}^k$.

nodes.name: Tight frame
nodes.statement: A collection $(\psi_\ell)$ joined as columns of $\Psi$ ($m\times m'$, $m<m'$) with $\Psi\Psi^T=I_m$, yielding the Parseval relation $\|x\|_2=\|\Psi^T x\|_2$ and reconstruction $x=\Psi(\Psi^T x)$.

nodes.name: Compressed Sensing Rate Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $(n,m_n)$ be problem sizes with $n<m_n$, $n\to\infty$, $m_n\sim A n^{\gamma}$, $\gamma>1$. For $0<p\le 1$ there is $C_p=C_p(A,\gamma)>0$ with $E_n(X_{p,m}(R)) \le C_p \cdot R \cdot (n/\log(m_n))^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Adaptive vs. nonadaptive equivalence
nodes.statement: For $0<p\le 1$, $R>0$, $E_n(X_{p,m}(R)) \le 2^{1/p}\cdot E_n^{\mathrm{Adapt}}(X_{p,m}(R))$.
conclusions: $E_n(X_{p,m}(R)) \le 2^{1/p} E_n^{\mathrm{Adapt}}(X_{p,m}(R))$ — adaptive sampling helps only by a constant

nodes.name: Equivalence of $E_n$ and Gel'fand $n$-width
nodes.statement: For $0<p\le 1$ and $R>0$: $d^n(X_{p,m}(R)) \le E_n(X_{p,m}(R)) \le 2^{1/p-1} \cdot d^n(X_{p,m}(R))$.
conclusions: $d^n \le E_n \le 2^{1/p-1} d^n$ — Gel'fand width and minimax error are equivalent up to factor $2^{1/p-1}$

nodes.name: Kashin-Garnaev-Gluskin (KGG)
nodes.statement: For all $n$ and $m>n$, $d_n(b_{2,m},\ell_\infty) \asymp (n/(1+\log(m/n)))^{-1/2}$.

nodes.name: Near-optimality of CS Information and $\ell_1$ minimization
nodes.statement: For $n<m_n\sim A n^\gamma$, $\gamma\ge 1$, $0<p\le 1$, the CS information operator $I_n^{\mathrm{CS}}$ obeys $E_n(I_n^{\mathrm{CS}},X_{p,m}(R)) \le C \cdot E_n(X_{p,m}(R))$ and the algorithm $A_{1,n}$ solving $(L_1)$ obeys $E_n(A_{1,n},I_n^{\mathrm{CS}},X_{p,m}(R)) \le C \cdot E_n(X_{p,m}(R))$.
assumptions: $I_n^{\mathrm{CS}}$ derives from CS matrices with parameters $(\eta_i),\rho$

nodes.name: Ubiquity of CS matrices
nodes.statement: For $(n,m_n)$ with $n\to\infty$, $m\sim A n^\gamma$, $\gamma\ge 1$, there exist $\eta_i>0$, $\rho>0$ depending only on $A,\gamma$ so that for each $\delta>0$ the proportion of $n\times m$ matrices satisfying CS1-CS3 with parameters $(\eta_i),\rho$ eventually exceeds $1-\delta$.
conclusions: $\exists\,\eta_i>0,\rho>0$ depending only on $A,\gamma$ such that the proportion of $\Phi$ satisfying CS1-CS3 tends to $1$

nodes.name: Near-optimality of widths under CS conditions
nodes.statement: If $\Phi_{n,m_n}$ obeys CS1-CS3 with constants $(\eta_i),\rho$ independent of $n$, then for each $p\in(0,1]$ there is $C=C(p,\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3,\rho,A,\gamma)$ with $w(\Phi_{n,m_n},b_{p,m_n}) \le C\cdot (n/\log(m/n))^{1/2-1/p}$ for $n>n_0$.
assumptions: $\Phi_{n,m_n}$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with parameters $(\eta_i),\rho$ independent of $n$

nodes.name: $\ell_1$/$\ell_0$ equivalence for sparse solutions
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with constants $\rho,(\eta_i)$, there is $\rho_0>0$ depending only on $\rho,(\eta_i)$ so that whenever some solution to $y=\Phi\theta$ has at most $\rho_0 n/\log(m)$ nonzeros, $(P_0)$ and $(P_1)$ have the same unique solution.
assumptions: some solution to $y=\Phi\theta$ has $\le \rho_0 n/\log(m)$ nonzeros
conclusions: $(P_0)$ and $(P_1)$ have the same unique solution

nodes.name: Near-optimality of Basis Pursuit for $0<p<1$
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with $(\eta_i),\rho$, there is $C=C(p,(\eta_i),\rho,A,\gamma)$ so that the solution $\hat{\theta}_{1,n}$ of $(P_1)$ with $y=\Phi\theta_0$ obeys $\|\theta_0-\hat{\theta}_{1,n}\|_2 \le C_p\,\|\theta_0\|_p \cdot (n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Random columns yield CS matrices
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi=\Phi_{n,m}$ have $m$ columns drawn i.i.d. uniformly from $\boldsymbol{S}^{n-1}$ with $n<m\sim A n^\gamma$, $\gamma>1$. There exist $\eta_i>0$, $\rho>0$ for which CS1-CS3 hold with overwhelming probability for large $n$, in fact $P(\Omega_n^c)\le \exp(-\beta n)$.
conclusions: $\exists\,\eta_i,\rho>0$ with CS1-CS3 holding for $\Phi$ with overwhelming probability

nodes.name: Alternative formulation (A1+A2 imply $\ell_1$ recovery rate)
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ obeys A1: $\nu(\Phi,J)<\eta_1$ for $|J|<\rho_1 n/\log(m_n)$, with $\eta_1<1/2$; and A2: $w(\Phi,b_{1,m_n}) \le \eta_2\,(n/\log(m_n))^{-1/2}$, then for $0<p\le 1$ and $\theta\in b_{p,m}$, the solution of $(P_1)$ obeys $\|\hat{\theta}_{1,n}-\theta\|_2 \le C\,(n/\log(m_n))^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Feasible-Point Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $y_n=I_n(x_0)$, $x_0\in X_{p,m}(R)$, $I_n$ optimal, and $\hat{x}\in \hat{X}_{p,R}(y_n)$. Then for $0<p\le 1$, $\|x_0-\hat{x}\|_2 \le 2\cdot E_n(X_{p,m}(R))$.

nodes.name: Concentration bound on nullspace
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with $\eta_i,\rho$, there is $\eta_0$ depending on $\eta_i$ so that $|J|\le \rho_1 n/\log(m)$ with $\rho_1\le \rho$ implies $\nu(\Phi,J) \le \eta_0\cdot \rho_1^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ stability lemma
nodes.statement:
Let $	heta_0\in\mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|	heta_0-1_J 	heta_0\|_1 \le \epsilon$ and $
u(\Phi,J)\le 
u_0<1/2$. Then the solution $\hat{	heta}_1$ of $(P_1)$ for $y=\Phi	heta_0$ satisfies $\|	heta_0-\hat{	heta}_1\|_1 \le 2\epsilon/(1-2
u_0)$.

nodes.name: Minimum eigenvalue control (CS1)
nodes.statement: For $n\le m_n\sim A n^\gamma$ and $\Omega_{n,m,\rho,\lambda}=\{\lambda_{\min}(\Phi_J^T\Phi_J)\ge \lambda, \forall |J|<\rho n/\log(m)\}$, for each $\lambda<1$ and sufficiently small $\rho>0$, $P(\Omega_{n,m,\rho,\lambda}) \to 1$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Per-subset eigenvalue large deviation
nodes.statement: For $J\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}$, the event $\Omega_{n,J}=\{\lambda_{\min}(\Phi_J^T\Phi_J)>\lambda<1\}$ satisfies $P(\Omega_{n,J}^c) \le \exp(-n\beta_1)$ uniformly in $|J|\le \rho_1 n$ for some $\beta_1>0$ and sufficiently small $\rho_1>0$.

nodes.name: Combining principle (union over subsets)
nodes.statement: If events $\Omega_{n,J}$ all obey $P(\Omega_{n,J}^c) \le \exp(-n\beta)$ for $|J|\le \rho n$, then for $\rho_1<\min(\beta,\rho)$ and $\beta_1<\beta-\rho_1$, $P\{\Omega_{n,J}^c \text{ for some }J\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}, |J|\le \rho_1 n/\log(m)\} \le \exp(-\beta_1 n)$.

nodes.name: Spherical sections (CS2 generic)
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega_n^2(\epsilon,\rho)$ be the event that every $\Phi_J$ with $|J|\le \rho n/\log(m)$ offers an $\epsilon$-isometry between $\ell_2(J)$ and $\ell_1^n$. For each $\epsilon>0$ there is $\rho(\epsilon)>0$ with $P(\Omega_n^2)\to 1$.

nodes.name: Per-subset $\epsilon$-isometry probability
nodes.statement: Choose $\delta$ with $(1-3\delta)(1-\delta)^{-1}\ge (1-\epsilon)^{1/2}$ and $(1+\delta)(1-\delta)^{-1}\le (1+\epsilon)^{1/2}$, and $\rho_1=\rho_1(\epsilon)$ with $\rho_1(1+2/\delta)<\delta^2 \cdot 2/\pi$. Then $\max_{|J|\le \rho_1 n} P(\Omega_{n,J}^c) \le 2\exp(-\beta(\epsilon) n(1+o(1)))$.

nodes.name: Uniform Sign-Pattern Embedding
nodes.statement: Fix $\delta>0$, $\tau<\delta^2/128$, $\epsilon_n=(\log(m_n/(\tau n)))^{-1/2}/4$. For sufficiently small $\rho_3>0$ there is an event $\Omega_n^3$ with $P(\Omega_n^3)\to 1$ on which, for each $|J|<\rho_3 n/\log(m)$ and $\sigma\in\Sigma_J$, there is $y$ with $\|y-\epsilon_n\sigma\|_2 \le \epsilon_n\delta\|\sigma\|_2$ and $|\langle\phi_i,y\rangle|\le 1$ for all $i\in J^c$.
conclusions: On $\Omega_n^3$ a small multiple $\epsilon_n\sigma$ of every sign pattern almost lies in the dual ball

nodes.name: Individual Sign-Pattern Embedding
nodes.statement: For $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $y_0=\epsilon_n\sigma$, the iterative algorithm (kill-and-project) produces $y$ with $|\langle\phi_i,y\rangle|\le 1$ for all $i$. With $\phi_i$ i.i.d. uniform on $\boldsymbol{S}^{n-1}$, on an event $\Omega_\sigma$ with $P(\Omega_\sigma^c)\le 2n\exp(-n\beta)$, $\|y-y_0\|_2 \le \delta\|y_0\|_2$.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit near-optimality (case $p=1$)
nodes.statement: If $I_n$ achieves $E_n(I_n,X_{1,m}(1)) \le C\cdot E_n(X_{1,m}(1))$, then Basis Pursuit $A_{1,n}(y_n)=\hat{x}_{1,n}$ achieves $E_n(I_n,A_{1,n},X_{1,m}(R)) \le 2C \cdot E_n(X_{1,m}(R))$ for all $R>0$.
assumptions: $I_n$ near-optimal in the sense $E_n(I_n,X_{1,m}(1))\le C E_n(X_{1,m}(1))$

nodes.name: Optimal recovery problem
nodes.statement: Given a class $X\subset\mathbb{R}^m$, design $(I_n,A_n)$ minimizing $\sup_{x\in X}\|x-A_n(I_n(x))\|_2$. The optimum is $E_n(X)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Optimal Recovery / IBC: Pinkus [5], Traub & Woziakowski [6]

nodes.name: Least-norm reconstruction $(P_p)$
nodes.statement: $\min_x \|\theta(x)\|_p$ subject to $y_n=I_n(x)$, where $\theta(x)=\Psi^T x$. Solution $\hat{x}_{p,n}$ is the feasible point of least $\ell_p$ transform-norm.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit $(P_1)$ / $(L_1)$
nodes.statement: $\min_\theta \|\theta\|_1$ subject to $\Phi\theta=y_n$ (equivalently $\min_x\|\Psi^T x\|_1$ s.t. $I_n(x)=y_n$). Convex; reformulates to a linear program with $A=[\Phi\;-\Phi]$, $z\ge 0$.

nodes.name: $\ell_0$ minimization $(P_0)$
nodes.statement: $\min \|\theta\|_0$ subject to $\Phi\theta=y$, where $\|\theta\|_0$ counts nonzeros. Combinatorial in general.

nodes.name: Width-restricted optimization $(Q_p)$
nodes.statement: $\sup \|\theta\|_2$ subject to $\Phi\theta=0$ and $\|\theta\|_p\le 1$. Its value equals $w(\Phi,b_{p,m})$.

nodes.name: Central algorithm
nodes.statement: Optimal OR/IBC reconstruction returning the Chebyshev center of the feasible set: $\hat{x}_n^* = \mathrm{center}(I_n^{-1}(y_n) \cap X_{p,m}(R))$.
output: Reconstruction $\hat{x}_n^*$ achieving minimax error when $I_n$ is optimal

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit (linear programming reconstruction)
nodes.statement: Solve $\min_\theta \|\theta\|_1$ s.t. $\Phi\theta=y_n$ via the LP $\min 1^T z$ s.t. $Az=y_n$, $z\ge 0$ where $A=[\Phi\;-\Phi]$; recover $\theta^*=u^*-v^*$, $\hat{x}_{1,n}=\Psi\theta^*$.

nodes.name: CS Information operator
nodes.statement: Build $I_n^{\mathrm{CS}}=\Phi\Psi^T$, where $\Phi$ is an $n\times m$ matrix with i.i.d. uniform columns on $\boldsymbol{S}^{n-1}$ (yielding CS1-CS3 with overwhelming probability) and $\Psi$ holds the basis/frame columns.
input: Basis or tight frame matrix $\Psi$ ($m\times m$ or $m\times m'$)
output: Measurements $y_n=I_n^{\mathrm{CS}}(x_0)$ used by the reconstruction algorithm

nodes.name: Iterative dual-feasibility (kill-and-project) algorithm
nodes.statement: Starting from $y_0=\epsilon_n\sigma$, iteratively identify violated indices $I_\ell=\{i: |\langle\phi_i,y_\ell\rangle|>t_\ell\}$ with $t_\ell=1-2^{-\ell-1}$ and project $y_{\ell+1}=y_0-P_{J_\ell}y_0$ until $I_\ell=\emptyset$; output $y$ is dual-feasible.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1 (Feasible-Point)
nodes.statement: By optimality of the central algorithm, the radius of $\hat{X}_{p,R}(y_n)$ equals the minimax error $E_n$. Apply the triangle inequality to $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{x}_n^*$ to get the factor-2 bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7 (CS-width bound)
nodes.statement: Set $J$ = top-$k$ indices of $\theta$ with $k=\lfloor \rho n/\log(m)\rfloor$. Use $\ell_p \to \ell_q$ tail bounds (I.2)/(II.4) on $\theta_{J^c}$, invoke CS3 then CS2 on $v=\Phi_J\theta_J$, then CS1 to bound $\|\theta_J\|_2$; combine.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (Gel'fand width / minimax equivalence)
nodes.statement: Lower bound $E_n\ge d^n$ from $d^n=\mathrm{radius}(\hat{X}_{p,R}(0))$. Upper bound: extreme points $x_\pm$ realizing the radius; the difference $\delta=(x_+-x_-)/2^{1/p}$ lies in $X_{p,m}(R)\cap V_n^\perp$ via the $p$-triangle inequality, so $\|\delta\|_2 \le d^n$, giving $E_n\le 2^{1/p-1} d^n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: For $p=1$, KGG + duality (I.6) + (I.4). For $0<p<1$, lower bound via Carl's entropy-Gel'fand inequality and entropy-number asymptotics; upper bound from Theorems 6 and 7 plus the Feasible-Point Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: For any adaptive algorithm there is a subspace $V_n^0$ on which all $x$ produce the same information; the minimax error on this subspace is at least $\inf_{V_n}\mathrm{radius}(V_n\cap X_{p,m}(R))=d^n(X_{p,m}(R))$. Compare with $E_n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8 ($\ell_1$/$\ell_0$ equivalence)
nodes.statement: Show $\nu(\Phi,J)<1/2$ implies $\theta$ is the unique $(P_1)$ minimizer; use Lemma 4.1 to bound $\nu(\Phi,J)\le \eta_0\rho_0^{1/2}<1/2$ when $|J|\le \rho_0 n/\log m$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1 (concentration)
nodes.statement: For $\beta\in\ker(\Phi)$, partition $\beta=[\beta_J,\beta_{J^c}]$. Setting $v=\Phi_J\beta_J$, invoke CS2-CS3 to bound $\|v\|_2$; CS1 bounds $\|\beta_J\|_2$; then $\|\beta_J\|_1\le\sqrt{|J|}\|\beta_J\|_2$ yields $\nu \le \eta_2\eta_3/\eta_1 \cdot \rho_1^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2 ($\ell_1$ stability)
nodes.statement: Set $\beta=\theta_0-\hat{\theta}\in\ker(\Phi)$. Bound $\|\beta\|_1 \le \|\beta_{J^c}\|_1/(1-\nu_0)$ via $\nu$. Use $\hat{\theta}$-optimality and triangle inequality to express $\|\beta_{J^c}\|_1\le \|1_J\beta\|_1+\|\theta_{0,J^c}\|_1$; substitute and solve for $\delta=\|\theta_0-\hat{\theta}\|_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9 (Basis Pursuit, $p<1$)
nodes.statement: Pick $J$ as top-$\rho_0 n/\log m$ entries of $\theta_0$. Apply (II.4) and Lemma 4.1 to control $\|\theta_0-1_J\theta_0\|_1$ and $\nu(\Phi,J)\le 1/4$. Use Lemma 4.2 to bound $\|\beta\|_1$, then convert to $\ell_2$ via $w(\Phi,b_{1,m})$ scaling: $\|\beta\|_2\le c\|\beta\|_1 (n/\log m)^{-1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3 (combining principle)
nodes.statement: Apply Boole's inequality $P(\cup_J \Omega_{n,J}^c) \le \#\mathcal{J}\cdot \exp(-\beta n)$. Use $\log\binom{m}{k}\le k\log m$ to get $\log(\#\mathcal{J})\le \rho_1 n$. Pick $\beta_1<\beta-\rho_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.6 (Uniform Sign-Pattern Embedding)
nodes.statement: Bound $\#\Sigma_J$ via VC theory; combine with Lemma 7.7 (per-pattern probability) and the union over $J$ and $\sigma$. The exponent $\beta-2\rho_3 > 0$ for $\rho_3<\beta/2$ gives $P(\Omega_n^{3,c})\to 0$ exponentially.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.7 (Individual Sign-Pattern Embedding)
nodes.statement: Define iterative-algorithm trajectory descriptors $\alpha_\ell,|I_\ell|$ with bounds $\delta_\ell, \nu_\ell$ geometric in $\omega$. Show $P(E_{\ell+1}^c | E_\ell)\le 2\exp(-\beta n)$ via Gaussian large-deviations bounds (Lemma 7.8) on $\sum Z_i^2 1_{|Z_i|>\tau_\ell}$. Telescope across $\ell\le n$.

nodes.name: Best $N$-term approximation rate
nodes.statement: $\|\theta-\theta_N\|_2 \le \zeta_{2,p}\cdot \|\theta\|_p \cdot (N+1)^{1/2-1/p}$ (eq. I.2).

nodes.name: Linear program reformulation of $(P_1)$
nodes.statement: $(LP)\;\min_z 1^T z$ s.t. $Az=y_n$, $z\ge 0$, with $A=[\Phi\;-\Phi]$; $\theta^*=u^*-v^*$ recovers $(P_1)$.

nodes.name: Sampling kernel form
nodes.statement: $\xi_i = \sum_{\ell=1}^m \Phi_{i,\ell}\,\phi_\ell$, $i=1,\ldots,n$ (eq. VI.1).

nodes.name: Bounded Variation model for images
nodes.statement: $f(x,y)$ on $[0,1]^2$ with $\int |\nabla f|\le R$. Wavelet coefficients per scale satisfy $\|\theta^{(j)}\|_1\le 4R$, giving an $\ell_1$ constraint.

nodes.name: Bump Algebra model for spectra
nodes.statement: Spectrum $f(t)=\sum_i a_i g((t-t_i)/s_i)$ with $\sum_i |a_i|\le R$. Smooth wavelet coefficients per scale obey $\|\theta^{(j)}\|_1 \le c R 2^{-j/2}$.

nodes.name: Compressed sensing for Bump Algebra
nodes.statement: With $j_0=j_1/3$, $n=c\cdot 2^{j_0}\log(2^{j_1})$ measurements suffice for $\|f-\hat{f}\|_2\le c\,2^{-j_1/2}$, comparable to classical $2^{j_1}$-sample rate; only $\sim m^{1/3}\log m$ samples needed.

nodes.name: Compressed sensing for Bounded Variation images
nodes.statement: With $j_0=j_1/2$ and $n=c\cdot 4^{j_0}\log^3(4^{j_1})$ Haar-based CS measurements, achieve $\|f-\hat f\|_2\le c\,2^{-j_1/2}$; only $\sim \sqrt{m}\log^3 m$ samples needed.

nodes.name: Compressed sensing for piecewise $C^2$ images with $C^2$ edges
nodes.statement: Curvelet coefficients satisfy $\|\theta^{(j)}\|_{w\ell_{2/3}}\le c(B,L)$. With $j_0=j_1/4$ and $n=c\cdot 4^{j_0}\log^{5/2}(4^{j_1})$, achieve $\|f-\hat f\|_2\le c\,2^{-j_1/2}$; only $\sim m^{1/4}\log^{5/2} m$ samples needed.

nodes.name: Tight-frame extension
nodes.statement: Theorems 7 and 9 only use the Parseval relation. Hence the same near-optimality results hold when $\Psi$ defines a tight frame (and even general frames, with constants involving the frame bounds).

nodes.name: Weak-$\ell_p$ extension
nodes.statement: Theorems 7 and 9 used only the tail estimate (V.1). They extend to spaces $Y_{p,m}(R)$ defined via weak-$\ell_p$ norms.

nodes.name: Partial Fourier ensemble (related work)
nodes.statement: Candès-Romberg-Tao [13] effectively prove A1 holds for the uniformly sampled partial Fourier ensemble; Gilbert et al. [12] suggest A2 holds with a nonuniform measure. These provide concrete constructions within the CS framework.
nodes.origin_citation: Candès, Romberg, Tao [13]; Gilbert et al. [12]; Candès & Tao [47]

nodes.name: Choose top-$k$ index set $J$
nodes.statement: For $\theta$ with $\Phi\theta=0$, let $J$ index the $k=\lfloor \rho n/\log(m)\rfloor$ largest entries of $\theta$ and write $\theta=[\theta_J,\theta_{J^c}]$.

nodes.name: Tail bounds on $\theta_{J^c}$
nodes.statement: Use (I.2) to get $\|\theta_{J^c}\|_2 \le \zeta_{2,p}(k+1)^{1/2-1/p}$, and the analogous $\ell_1$-tail bound $\|\theta_{J^c}\|_1 \le \zeta_{1,p}(k+1)^{1-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Apply CS3 then CS2 on $v=\Phi_J\theta_J$
nodes.statement: Set $v=\Phi_J\theta_J=-\Phi_{J^c}\theta_{J^c}\in V_J$. CS3 gives $\|\theta_{J^c}\|_1 \ge Q_{J^c}(-v) \ge \eta_3/\sqrt{\log(m/n)}\,\|v\|_1$; CS2 gives $\|v\|_1 \ge \eta_2 \sqrt{n}\,\|v\|_2$. Combine to bound $\|v\|_2 \le c_1 (n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Apply CS1 to bound $\|\theta_J\|_2$
nodes.statement: By CS1, $\|\theta_J\|_2 \le \|\Phi_J\theta_J\|_2/\eta_1 = \|v\|_2/\eta_1 \le c_2 (n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Combine pieces and conclude
nodes.statement: $\|\theta\|_2 \le \|\theta_J\|_2 + \|\theta_{J^c}\|_2 \le C(n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$ with $C=\zeta_{1,p}\rho^{1-1/p}/(\eta_1\eta_2\eta_3) + \zeta_{2,p}\rho^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound from entropy numbers
nodes.statement: By Carl's theorem, $d^n(b_{p,m}) \ge c\,e_n(b_{p,m})$, and $e_n(b_{p,m}) \asymp (n/\log(m/n))^{1/2-1/p}$ (Schütt; Kuhn).

nodes.name: Upper bound via Theorems 6 and 7
nodes.statement: Theorem 6 furnishes a CS matrix $\Phi$ with overwhelming probability; Theorem 7 yields $d^n(b_{p,m}) \le w(\Phi,b_{p,m}) \le c(n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Lift width to error via Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Apply the Feasible-Point Lemma 3.1 to convert the width bound to a bound on $E_n(X_{m,p}(R))$, giving $E_n(X_{m,p}(1)) \le 2 d^n(b_{p,m})$ and the rate $E_n \asymp (n/\log(m/n))^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Case $p=1$ (KGG via duality)
nodes.statement: For $p=1$, the result also follows directly from Garnaev-Gluskin via duality (I.6) and the $E_n$-Gel'fand width equivalence (I.4).

nodes.name: Choose $J$ as top-$\rho_0 n/\log m$ entries
nodes.statement: Let $\eta_0$ be from Lemma 4.1, $\rho_0=\min(\rho,(4\eta_0)^{-2})$. Index $J$ = $\rho_0 n/\log(m)$ largest amplitude entries of $\theta_0$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\theta_0-1_J\theta_0\|_1$ and $\nu(\Phi,J)$
nodes.statement: $\|\theta_0\|_p\le R$ and (II.4) give $\|\theta_0-1_J\theta_0\|_1 \le \xi_{1,p}\,R\,|J|^{1-1/p}$. Lemma 4.1 gives $\nu(\Phi,J) \le \eta_0\rho_0^{1/2} \le 1/4$.

nodes.name: Apply $\ell_1$ stability (Lemma 4.2)
nodes.statement: Lemma 4.2 yields $\|\beta\|_1 \le c R |J|^{1-1/p}$ where $\beta=\hat{\theta}-\theta_0\in\ker(\Phi)$.

nodes.name: Convert $\ell_1$ bound to $\ell_2$ via width
nodes.statement: $\delta=\beta/\|\beta\|_1\in\ker(\Phi)$ has $\|\delta\|_1=1$, hence $\|\delta\|_2 \le c(n/\log m)^{-1/2}$. By homogeneity, $\|\beta\|_2 \le c R(n/\log m)^{1/2-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Define algorithm trajectory descriptors
nodes.statement: Define $\alpha_\ell=\|y_\ell-y_{\ell-1}\|_2$ and $|I_\ell|$ for the kill-and-project iteration. Set bounds $\delta_{\ell;n}=\|y_0\|_2\omega^\ell$ and $\nu_{\ell;n}=n\lambda_0\epsilon_n^2 \omega^{2\ell+2}/4$ with $\omega=\min(1/2,\delta/2,\omega_0)$.

nodes.name: Define event chain $E_\ell$
nodes.statement: $E_\ell = \{\alpha_j\le\delta_j, j\le\ell;\;|I_j|\le\nu_j, j\le\ell-1\}$. On $\Omega_\sigma=\cap_{\ell=1}^n E_\ell$, $\|y-y_0\|_2 \le \|y_0\|_2 \delta$.

nodes.name: Reduce to Gaussian large-deviations
nodes.statement: On $E_\ell$, $\lambda_{\min}(\Phi_{I_\ell}^T\Phi_{I_\ell})>\lambda_0$. Express $P\{F_{\ell+1}^c | G_\ell, E_\ell\}$ in terms of $\sum Z_i^2 1_{|Z_i|>\tau_\ell}$ for $Z_i$ i.i.d. $N(0,1)$. Apply Lemma 7.8 with $\tau_\ell^2=n v_\ell^2$ and $\Delta_\ell$ from $\nu_\ell, \delta_\ell$.

nodes.name: Bound exponent and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $\beta(\tau;\delta)=(\delta/2)^2/32-\tau$, get $\beta>0$ for $\tau<\delta^2/128$ and $P\{F_{\ell+1}^c|G_\ell,E_\ell\}\le \exp(-n\beta)$. Telescope: $P(\Omega_\sigma^c) \le 2n\exp(-n\beta)$.

nodes.name: Reformulate as LP
nodes.statement: Form $A=[\Phi\;-\Phi]$ ($n\times 2m$). Set up the LP $\min_z 1^T z$ subject to $Az=y_n$, $z\ge 0$.

nodes.name: Solve LP (interior point / simplex)
nodes.statement: Compute $z^*\in\mathbb{R}^{2m}_+$ via interior-point methods (or simplex). For very large underdetermined problems ($n=8192$, $m=262144$) this remains tractable.

nodes.name: Recover $\theta^*$ and $\hat{x}_{1,n}$
nodes.statement: Partition $z^*=[u^*\;v^*]$ and set $\theta^*=u^*-v^*$, $\hat{x}_{1,n}=\Psi\theta^*$.

nodes.name: Initialize $y_0=\epsilon_n\sigma$ and $\ell=0$
nodes.statement: Set $y_0=\epsilon_n\sigma$. Compute $I_0=\{i: |\langle\phi_i,y_0\rangle|>1/2\}$ and $y_1=y_0-P_{I_0}y_0$.

nodes.name: Iterate kill-and-project loop
nodes.statement: While $I_\ell\ne\emptyset$: set $t_\ell=1-2^{-\ell-1}$, $I_\ell=\{i: |\langle\phi_i,y_\ell\rangle|>t_\ell\}$, $J_\ell=I_0\cup\cdots\cup I_\ell$, $y_{\ell+1}=y_0-P_{J_\ell}y_0$. Termination at $\ell^*\le n$.

nodes.name: Return dual-feasible $y$
nodes.statement: Output $y=y_{\ell^*}$ satisfying $|\langle\phi_i,y\rangle|\le 1-2^{-\ell^*-1}$ for all $i$.
